title: SCIM provisioning: consistency window, deprovision escrow and retry playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a production-ready SCIM provisioning flow that reduces accidental deprovisioning impact by introducing a configurable consistency window and an escrow/soft-delete stage. The work covers user and group create/update/delete semantics, idempotent retries across partial failures, integration with audit-logging, and operator-driven restore paths. Goal: make SCIM-driven deprovision operations safe for large tenants and noisy systems while preserving eventual reconciliation correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning: create/update semantics for user and group objects must be idempotent across retries (duplicate creation/update requests don't create duplicates or leave dangling refs)
Deprovision escrow: deletes from SCIM are soft-deleted into an escrow state for a configurable retention window (default 72h) before irreversible removal
Consistency window: changes include a per-tenant stabilization window (configurable) that batches rapid successive deltas to avoid flapping and reconcile loops
Retries: exponential backoff with jitter and tenant-rate-awareness must be implemented; system can resume interrupted bulk operations without duplication
Audit logs: every SCIM action (incoming request, transitional state change, final deletion) is emitted to audit logs with an immutable request_id and tenant_id
Restore workflow: operators can list escrowed objects and restore them with original IDs; restoring replays provisioning flows and emits audit events
Monitoring/Alerts: runbooks added and dashboards surface escrow growth, retry error rates, and deprovision throughput per tenant
implementation_notes: Introduce escrow table for soft-deletes with columns (tenant_id, scim_id, object_type, payload_snapshot, deleted_at, ttl_expires_at, request_id)
Use request_id derived from SCIM PATCH/DELETE request signature to enable idempotent replay and de-duplication
Delta stabilization: on receiving a SCIM change, start a per-tenant timer (stabilization window). Collapse sequential ops for same scim_id within window into a single reconcile action
Backoff: implement token-bucket per-tenant throttles plus capped exponential backoff with randomized jitter to avoid herd retries
Observability: add trace propagation for request_id and include audit events to ELK/Kafka topic 'audit.scim'
Compatibility: support existing enterprise customers using immediate deletes via opt-out flag (force=true) during migration period
design_decisions: Escrow vs tombstone: choose escrow with TTL and operator restore UI over permanent tombstones to balance auditability and storage cost
Consistency window default: 72 hours chosen after sampling tenant change patterns (median burst 1-6 hours); configurable per-tenant to support aggressive SSO flows
Idempotency key: SHA256 of (tenant_id|scim_operation|external_request_timestamp) as request_id to be forwarded and stored
Retry policy: per-tenant token bucket rate limits to protect downstream identity connectors and avoid cascading failures
plan_milestones: M1: Schema + Escrow table + migration script (2026-03-05)
M2: Idempotency request_id plumbing + basic retry loop (2026-03-12)
M3: Delta stabilization timer and batching operator (2026-03-19)
M4: Audit log integration + dashboards + runbook (2026-03-26)
M5: Rollout to canary tenants + operator restore UI (2026-04-02)
M6: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy immediate-delete path (2026-04-16)
risks: Increased storage for escrowed objects for large tenants — mitigation: TTL compaction job and size-based retention policy
Behavioral divergence: tenant expectations for immediate deletes — mitigation: opt-out flag and migration docs
Operational complexity for operators restoring objects that have downstream side effects — mitigation: automated dependency checks and pre-restore dry-run
Race conditions if multiple SCIM connectors operate concurrently for same tenant — mitigation: strongly-ordered reconcile by scim_id and request_id dedupe
dependencies: ENG-41022: audit pipeline schema update (must land before audit.scim emission)
ENG-45100: operator console: escrow browse/restore UI
SEC-990: security review for request_id hashing and PII in payload snapshots
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotent create/update/delete flows
Integration test with mock identity connector that simulates transient failures and slow responses
Chaos test: concurrent deletes + updates across two connector workers for same tenant to validate dedupe and stabilization
E2E Canary: enable escrow for two low-risk tenants and exercise restore flow
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal staging with full traffic; monitor escrow queue length and retry error rates
Phase 1: canary 5 tenants with high-change rates (opt-in) for 1 week
Phase 2: open for all new tenants by default; existing tenants must opt-in or be migrated with a communication plan
Emergency kill-switch: feature flag to short-circuit escrow and revert to legacy immediate delete in case of severe regressions
